name: agency-netsuite
label: NetSuite & ERP Agency Partners
description: Targets decision-makers at NetSuite SIs, Oracle partners, and ERP implementation agencies whose clients need eCommerce built alongside their NetSuite deployment. AOTT's primary criteria for staff augmentation with ERP consultancies.
_note: AOTT's sweet spot is staff augmentation with ERP consulting/implementation agencies. The pitch: ERP agencies don't carry eCommerce expertise in-house — we fill that layer. Target: decision-makers at NetSuite SIs, Oracle partners, and ERP implementation consultancies who serve clients that need Shopify or SuiteCommerce built alongside their NetSuite deployment.
_company_type_signals_note: These signals must be platform-specific to count toward agency boost. Generic words like 'Solutions', 'Services', 'Digital', 'Advisory' alone are not sufficient — they must appear alongside a platform keyword.
_target_roles_note: Operator feedback 2026-08-18: after ~40 abbreviated runs, the US/UK/CA/AU pool of unmined decision-makers at NetSuite partner firms was showing sub-6% hot rates across two consecutive runs, with the clearest exec-level candidate at each freshly-discovered firm repeatedly turning out to be already-seen. Broadened target_roles and target_locations below to widen the addressable pool rather than keep re-mining the same narrow set of titles/geos. Added roles reflect titles that scored hot/warm this session via seniority_match + agency boost despite not being an exact target_roles hit (Managing Partner, President, COO, Chief Growth Officer, Director of ERP, Business Development Director) — making them exact role matches should lift borderline-warm cases into hot where seniority and platform fit are already strong.
_target_industries_note: LinkedIn industry field alone is not sufficient — must be combined with platform-specific domain signals.
_target_locations_note: Operator feedback 2026-08-18: broadened beyond the original US/UK/CA/AU set to other high-income, English-business-fluent markets where this session repeatedly found genuine (not yet AOTT-competing offshore-delivery) NetSuite Alliance Partners with real decision-makers: Ireland (Redfaire, Eaton Square), Netherlands (Bring IT), Germany (Primus Delphi — German-speaking Oracle/NetSuite partner), Singapore (PointStar, JPS-iQ, HAND Global), New Zealand (Fusion5). Deliberately did not add India/Philippines/LATAM — those markets are where the same partner firms' offshore delivery ICs sit, and per this session's evidence those individuals already correctly classify cold on role/seniority grounds regardless of location, so adding them as target locations would mostly just relax a filter that isn't the actual bottleneck there.
_retail_brand_guidance: A lead at a retail/DTC/consumer brand (not an agency or SI) qualifies as warm or above ONLY when their company is a confirmed Shopify or NetSuite/SuiteCommerce user. The platform signal must be strong and current. Without it, classify as cold regardless of seniority.
_excluded_employers_note: AOTT sells staff augmentation TO the partner ecosystem, never to the platform vendors themselves. Anyone whose CURRENT employer is a platform vendor is not a lead: they have internal delivery orgs and do not buy external agency capacity. Detect from the headline when company fields are null: 'at Oracle', 'at NetSuite', '@ Shopify', 'Oracle Consulting', 'Oracle Cloud Applications'. Watch for Oracle-internal titles — 'Consulting Practice Director', 'Consulting Project Director', 'Head of Consulting Services' with Oracle context (or no partner-company context at all) are vendor employees, not partner-agency staff. Classify excluded-employer leads as cold and cap score at 25 regardless of seniority — this exclusion overrides company_type_signals and seniority_signals. Do not drop them from output; the operator can still manually approve a rare vendor-side contact from the cold tier. Two adjacent exclusions, also cold: (a) mega-SIs with in-house delivery at scale (Accenture, Deloitte, Capgemini, IBM, Infosys, TCS, Wipro, Cognizant, Coforge) — cap at 40; (b) in-house IT/ERP/digital-transformation leaders at end-user enterprises or unrelated software vendors (banks, insurers, Unit4, BlackLine, etc.) — cap at 30. The buyer must work at an agency, SI, or consultancy whose BUSINESS is delivering NetSuite/ERP projects for clients, sized boutique-to-mid-market like the reference_companies.
_excluded_companies_note: Operator feedback 2026-07-16: never surface anyone from these firms in any tier. Unlike excluded_employers (surfaced cold), these are dropped entirely at Step 2 — skip the result AND write it to seen.json so it never resurfaces. Detect from headline naming the firm. Operator feedback 2026-06-09 (SuiteDB), 2026-07-27 (Seibert Consulting Group), 2026-08-06 (AnagramDev), and 2026-08-06 (FullClarity — no fit for AOTT despite being a genuine NetSuite partner): absolutely no interest in engaging with these agencies under any circumstances — treat as a hard block, not a scoring signal. Operator feedback 2026-08-12: N2Lab is now an active AOTT client relationship — exclude from all criteria and never surface as a new lead, regardless of fit.
_sap_note: Operator feedback 2026-07-09: SAP-related leads are out of scope entirely — no business there. This is broader than excluded_employers: SAP partner consultancies, SAP implementation practices, and in-house SAP program leaders are all non-buyers. A generic ERP signal that resolves to SAP does not pass the domain gate.
_search_terms_note: QUERY-BUILDING RULE for Step 2: never pair a bare platform name with a role. 'Oracle consulting' matches Oracle's own Consulting org. Every query must include a partner/agency/implementation/reseller qualifier alongside the platform name (e.g. 'NetSuite alliance partner', 'SuiteCommerce agency') so results skew toward people whose employer partners with the platform rather than the vendor's own staff.
